question: Why do the people who sing, play and listen to music most also get the most tunes stuck in their heads?
answer: Because an earworm is musical memory rehearsing itself. Lassi Liikkanen surveyed over 12,000 Finns: about nine in ten had a stuck tune at least weekly, and frequency rose with how much music people played, sang and heard. More tunes stocked and used means more to replay. A fuller jukebox plays more often.
move: Whatever fills the hours supplies what the idle mind replays later.
ask: What am I feeding my mind all day that it keeps replaying when I am idle?
reference: Liikkanen, Musical activities predispose to involuntary musical imagery, Psychology of Music, 2012
